identity.name: Fen Vikutā
identity.bio: An Arasaka researcher raised in Japan, born to a Japanese researcher and a Night City-born intelligence operative. Both parents were Saburo loyalists. Fen carries their legacy into a life stripped of corporate protection.

build.human_bonus: Standard human: +1 to all six attributes.

attributes.name: Body
attributes.description: Force, lifting, Athletics and melee strength.

attributes.name: Reflexes
attributes.description: Initiative, evasion, stealth and ranged weapon handling.

attributes.name: Cool
attributes.description: Program execution, composure, influence and mental resistance.

proficiencies.tools_note: Cybertech kit proficient; kit not owned.

resources.hp_note: Full health. Superficial cuts and bruises.
resources.rest_note: One tier-1 slot returns after a Short Rest or Long Rest. Neither automatically restores HP.

programs.name: Short Circuit
programs.summary: Overload exposed circuitry with a precise destructive packet.
programs.effect: Make one ranged program attack (+5) against a visible compatible powered target. On a hit, deal 1d10 Electrical damage to physical HP, or 1d10 Data damage to ICE integrity in software mode. At total levels 5, 11 and 17, send 2, 3 and 4 packets respectively, each with its own attack and target. No Cool modifier is added to damage at level 1.
programs.requirements: Wirelessly target powered Cyberware or an electronic actor/object within range; its circuitry supplies the destructive current. Software mode targets reachable ICE and uses virtual AC. Declare each packet’s mode before attacking.
programs.scaling: Output Amplifier is a possible level-2 Firmware Upgrade, not currently installed.

programs.name: Decoy Projection
programs.summary: Forge an image or sound through nearby presentation hardware.
programs.effect: Create one sound, from a whisper to a scream, or a static object image within a 5-foot cube. An image adds no sound, smell, light or solidity. Physical interaction reveals an image. A creature examining it with an action can identify the deception with Intelligence (Investigation) DC 13. Ends on dismissal (action), replacement by another execution or after 1 minute.
programs.requirements: A speaker for sound, or a suitable display, projector or sensory interface for the image, reachable wirelessly within range. The device must be able to produce the chosen effect.
programs.scaling: Utility; no slot and no level-based increase.

programs.name: Vulnerability Tag
programs.summary: Mark a neural weakness and exploit it with each successful attack.
programs.effect: Choose a visible reachable neural or robotic target; no initial save. Your attacks against it deal an extra 1d6 damage matching the triggering attack’s primary damage type on a hit. Choose one ability: its checks have disadvantage, not its Saving Throws. After it reaches 0 HP, transfer the tag to another legal target with a Bonus Action on a subsequent turn. A software-target mode can mark reachable ICE; the rider on a Data attack deals Data damage. For mixed attacks, the direct base damage is primary; if the base is mixed, use its first printed component.
programs.requirements: Wirelessly target integrated neural Cyberware or a robotic system within range. Software mode targets a reachable ICE instance. Maintain Concentration for the printed duration.
programs.scaling: Tier 3–4: up to 8 hours. Tier 5+: up to 24 hours. Tier 2: still 1 hour. Firmware clearance can end it.

features.name: Burst Processing
features.summary: 2 Utilities · 1 of 2 Programs chosen · 1 Execution Slot
features.detail: Cool is your program ability. Attack +5; save DC 13. Known software is fixed between levels. One tier-1 slot returns on a Short Rest or Long Rest. Utilities consume no slot. One Concentration program at a time; on damage make a Constitution save (+2), DC 10 or half damage, whichever is higher. After a Bonus Action program, other programs on that turn may only be action utilities. All programs need their real equipment and access.

features.name: Research Network
features.summary: Find the likely archive, department or specialist for a technical question
features.detail: You know how to identify the likely department or archive for a technical question and how to request access. Credentials, trust, time and actual access still matter. Former employment does not restore revoked permissions.

cyberware.name: Cyclops Civic C2
cyberware.summary: Cyan iris shells · Chyron HUD · two empty option slots per eye
cyberware.detail: Cyclops International Civic C2 replacement eyes, a second-hand matched pair fitted by Maelstrom. Human-shaped housings with cyan iris shells provide ordinary vision and a built-in Chyron HUD. Each eye has two empty optical option slots. Persistent advertising crowds the display, imposing disadvantage on sight-based Perception until replacement. Passive Perception: sight 7; other senses 12.

cyberware.name: Rocklin Augmentics NP-1
cyberware.summary: Exposed ear-mounted controller; basic interface functions only
cyberware.detail: Decades-old Rocklin cyberware patched together by Maelstrom. A bulky external casing hooks around the right ear, connected to an implanted neural anchor. Two empty exposed adapter sockets accept shards; a basic personal-link lead exits beside the upper-neck mount. Fen conceals the casing beneath his hair. When the distinctive casing is visible, observers have advantage on Perception checks to recognise or identify Fen using it as an identifying feature. Concealing it beneath his hair removes that visual cue. Exposed connections are vulnerable to snagging, grabbing or direct damage. Retains a biomonitor, basic holophone/HUD, neural link, virtuality display and five empty neuralware option connections.

inventory.name: Clothing
inventory.summary: Black-and-red Arasaka outfit · long coat, shirt, trousers, gloves and boots
inventory.detail: A tailored, calf-length black coat with structured shoulders, a high collar, red edging and red lining visible through the split hem. A red Arasaka emblem marks the left chest. Beneath it: a fitted black high-neck shirt with narrow red trim, tapered black trousers, and a black belt with a rectangular metal buckle and red straps at the hips. Black full-finger gloves have red back panels and wrist straps; mid-calf black boots have multiple buckle straps with red toes, soles and side panels. Scuffed and dirty from the escape and rough handling, but wearable. Pockets empty.

journal.title: Fen Vikutā
journal.body: Raised in Japan. Former Arasaka researcher specialising in engram modelling, cognitive systems and laboratory software.

rules.rests: Short Rest: 1 hour, restores Contractor slots. Long Rest: 8 hours under the normal 2014 rules, restores class resources and half total Hit Dice (minimum 1), but no automatic HP.
rules.convalescence: Once per 24 hours, after 8 hours of rest with food, water and appropriate first aid, spend up to one quarter of total Hit Dice rounded up (half in a stocked clinic). At level 1 this is one d8 + 2, minimum 0 HP. Critical injuries must be treated first.
rules.injuries: The first damaging drop from positive HP to 0 in an encounter causes one critical injury. A critical hit above 0 does not. Standard injuries require treatment and 7 qualifying convalescence days; major injuries associated with a failed death save require surgery and 21 days.
rules.intrusion: Quickhacks upload wirelessly within their printed range. Target identification and upload are part of execution; resolve the Program’s attack or Saving Throw. Utilities are at will; tiered Programs spend an Execution Slot. Effects need a physical source: powered Cyberware for an overload, fuel and ignition for a combustion blast, or a chemical payload for toxins.
rules.capacity: Native Neural Tolerance = max(4, 6 + Constitution modifier + Cool modifier) = 11. Add earned Adaptation, currently 0. Current Load: 0. Load above tolerance creates overload risk. Baseline replacements are Load 0.
rules.progression: Level 2 at 300 total XP: two tier-1 slots, three known programs and two Firmware Upgrades. Level 3: Interface Platform.
rules.secured_intrusion: Use Intelligence (Technology), currently +4, for meaningful obstacles such as protected files or persistent access. Routine work needs no roll; complex jobs can involve several distinct checks. This costs no Execution Slot. Active opposition can instead become a deep-dive combat encounter using normal initiative, actions, attacks and saves, with suitable deep-dive equipment.
